paras: The mob pursuit of Henry Williams took place in Cincinnati, Ohio, on August 12, 1895, when a crowd chased Williams, a Black man, through the streets after his companion Thomas Jones was accused of stabbing a white man. The crowd, put at 300 in the chase and about 2,000 at the depot, knocked Williams down before police held it back by drawing their pistols. The story ran as a short wire item in papers from Texas to Minnesota, one of which headlined it as a rescue by the police.

According to a Cincinnati dispatch dated August 12, Thomas Jones, described as "colored," and James Daley, white, had met the previous day at the room of a white woman. Her name was printed as Emma Conley, Mary Conley or Mary Cennolly, depending on the paper. Daley drove Jones away on that occasion.

The next day Jones returned to the woman's room with another Black man, Henry Williams, and was reported to have attacked and stabbed Daley. Jones and Williams then ran out of the building; officers caught Jones, while a mob of 300 people took after Williams.

In the fuller version of the dispatch, Williams grabbed bricks as he ran and hurled them back into the crowd. At the depot "fully two thousand people" surrounded him, and a brakeman knocked him down with a boulder. Officers then had to show their pistols to keep the crowd back.

The fuller dispatch and an Ohio news digest described Daley as "fatally stabbed," though no report of his death appears in the coverage. The coverage does not say whether Williams was hurt badly, whether he was arrested, or what charges, if any, Jones faced, and no report of a trial was found.

All of the known coverage came from a single wire dispatch printed in white newspapers on August 13, in a short form in the Fort Worth Gazette and a longer form in the Indianapolis Journal and the St. Paul Daily Globe. Headlines differed in emphasis: the Gazette's "Over a Woman. White Man and a Negro Engage in Fatal Quarrel" centered the stabbing, the Journal's "Negro Chased by a Mob" centered the pursuit, and the Globe's "Saved by the Police. Negro Rescued From a Mob of 2,000 People" centered the officers' intervention. The Globe printed the same item twice, on its first and second pages.

Two days later, a weekly in Napoleon, Ohio, reduced the story to a single line in its crimes column, naming Daley as "white" and Jones as "colored" and omitting the mob altogether. No account of the episode was found in the Black press.

reader.title: Mob pursuit of Henry Williams in Cincinnati
bases: A wire dispatch reports a crowd of 300, swelling to about 2,000, chasing Henry Williams through Cincinnati after a stabbing, with a brakeman knocking him down with a boulder before officers held the crowd back at pistol point; no killing or explicit lynching threat is reported (A1, A2, A3).

All accounts are versions of one Cincinnati dispatch dated Aug. 12 (A1, A2, A3, A4), and the only other item (A5) is a one-line digest of the stabbing; no local, Black-press or follow-up report was found.

accounts.label: Wire report (short form)
accounts.gist: Jones stabbed Daly after a quarrel at a white woman's room; officers caught Jones, a mob of 300 chased Williams, and officers showed pistols to keep the crowd back.

accounts.label: Wire report (full form)
accounts.gist: Adds that Daley was 'fatally stabbed', that Williams hurled bricks back at his pursuers, that some 2,000 people surrounded him at the depot, and that a brakeman knocked him down with a boulder before officers drew pistols on the crowd.

accounts.label: Ohio news digest
accounts.gist: Reports only that Daley, white, was fatally stabbed by Jones, colored, at Cincinnati.

framing.detail: The Fort Worth Gazette headed the short wire 'Over a Woman. White Man and a Negro Engage in Fatal Quarrel', framing the stabbing rather than the mob.

The Indianapolis Journal headed the full wire 'Negro Chased by a Mob' and the St. Paul Globe 'Saved by the Police. Negro Rescued From a Mob of 2,000 People', foregrounding the crowd and the officers' intervention.
An Ohio weekly reduced the story to a one-line racial label item on the stabbing in its crimes column, omitting the mob.

conflicts.note: Telegraphic variants of one dispatch; none is better evidence.
The short form's headline still says 'Fatal Quarrel'; no report of Daley's death was found.
Not a contradiction: the full text gives 300 for the chase and 2,000 for the crowd at the depot; the short form stops before the depot.

record_check.dossier: 1895-08-12: the dispatch dated Aug. 12 places the stabbing and chase 'Today'; Aug. 11 was the earlier meeting at the woman's room.
Henry Williams only; Thomas Jones is the man accused of the stabbing, who was caught by officers and is not reported as attacked by the mob.
Stabbing of James Daley, white, attributed to Thomas Jones; Williams was his companion.
A mob of 300, growing to about 2,000 at the depot; a brakeman knocked Williams down with a boulder.
Williams knocked down with a boulder (extent of injury not reported).
1: James Daley stabbed ('fatally' per the full wire text); no report of his death found.

record_check.record: After a white man was stabbed, officers arrested Jones while a mob of 300 chased Black man Henry Williams; officers drew pistols to hold it back.
record_check.dossier: Accurate as far as it goes, but omits the crowd of about 2,000 at the depot, the brakeman's boulder and Williams's thrown bricks.

info: The stabbing and mob chase occurred on the day of the Aug. 12 dispatch ('Today'); the first meeting at the woman's room, when Daley drove Jones away, was the day before ('Yesterday').
Cincinnati; the chase ended at 'the depot'.
Henry Williams, described as 'another negro' who accompanied Thomas Jones, was chased by the mob and knocked down.
Thomas Jones, 'colored', was reported to have attacked and stabbed James Daley (Daly), white, at the room of a white woman; Williams is described as Jones's companion, not as the one who stabbed.
A mob or crowd that took after Williams; a brakeman knocked him down. Their race is not stated.
